about: Every dimension the Ford build uses, with its source (an id in references.json), where in it, and the text it stands on (quote), which sources.py finds in the fetched copy. Values are in the source's own units; the build converts (1 ft = 0.3048 m). Where sources disagree, every value is recorded, with the one the model uses and why. Positions no source states are measured from the imagery and photos and go in layout, each saying what it was fitted to.

length.use: neither: the deck plan is measured off noaa2022, and the length follows
length.note: 1,092 ft is also the Nimitz's figure in the same tables. The orthos measure the flight deck at about 331-334 m, which fits 1,092 ft (332.8 m); what the 1,106 ft figure measures is not stated.

waterline.note: relays the Naval Vessel Register's withdrawn field; the same as the Nimitz's

deck.also: airlant ("Flight Deck Width : 256 feet"); globalsecurity ("Extreme Beam 256 ft")

navigational.note: its metric 7.8 m is wrong: 39 ft is 11.9 m. Decision 23: the model floats at her deployed load, read from the draught marks in deployed photos and checked against this.

area.use: a check only: the planform measured off noaa2022 gives its own area
area.note: the totals disagree; each puts the Ford about 2-10% above the Nimitz.

form.quote: same hull form as the CVN 68 Nimitz class
form.also: dote2019 ("same hull form as the CVN 68 Nimitz-class"); crs ("uses the basic Nimitz-class hull form")
form.note: no public lines, offsets or tank reports for CVN-68/77/78: the underwater hull is shaped from the 2013 dry-dock photos, at 1 m (decision 10)

deployed.where: stem draught marks, at the waterline
deployed.method: the waterline lies 0.25-0.35 ft below the foot of the 38 (95 px per foot in a 2x crop of x 900-1400, y 4650-5200); the 8's reflection fixes the water
deployed.note: forward draught only: no stern marks have been read, so the trim is unknown. A second deployed reading, DVIDS 9628694 (Souda Bay, 22-23 Feb 2026), gives about 37 ft 7 in; the homecoming of 16 May 2026 (DVIDS 9688116) about 34 ft, extrapolated past fouled numerals, at the end of a deployment. Decision 23 floats the model at the deployed draught; the navigational maximum is 39 ft (overall.draught.navigational).

boot.where: stem, top edge of the black boot-topping
boot.method: 0.8 ft above the foot of the 41 numeral in the same crop
boot.note: where the black waterline band meets the grey at the stem (decision 17)

length.quote: 60 feet long at the flight deck base

height.note: above the flight deck; whether this includes the mast is not stated

placement.quote: 140 feet further aft and 3 feet further outboard than previous carriers
placement.note: relative to an unnamed earlier carrier, so the island is placed from the imagery; this is a check

taller.quote: stands 20 feet taller than islands on previous aircraft carriers

length.quote: It measures 85 feet long and 52 feet wide
length.note: one starboard elevator, "the third and final aircraft elevator" installed (its image is named Ford_Elevator_1): elevator 1, which measures 26.0-26.4 m along its outboard side. Elevator 2 measures 27.05 m and elevator 3 25.89 m (references/research/deck).

width.quote: It measures 85 feet long and 52 feet wide
width.note: one starboard elevator, "the third and final aircraft elevator" installed (its image is named Ford_Elevator_1): elevator 1, which measures 26.0-26.4 m along its outboard side. Elevator 2 measures 27.05 m and elevator 3 25.89 m (references/research/deck).

measured.where: layout.elevators: elevator 1's outline off noaa2022, its inboard corner 0.03 m across in dvids7694421, its outboard edge the orthophoto's (references/research/deck, match)

width.use: measured: the platform meets the deck opening the photos see. 52 ft (15.85 m) is 0.52 m less, more than its rounding (0.15 m) or the imagery's fit (0.1-0.6 m on one side) explains; what the published figure measures (the platform inside its edge fittings, say) is not stated.

elevators.note: where each sits is measured off the imagery: two to starboard forward of the island and one to port (pms378 slide 3's top view; noaa2022).

engines.value: four engines and three wires, as CVN 76 and CVN 77
engines.quote: consisting of four engines and three wires
engines.note: the planned positions were similar to CVN 76's and 77's; the fourth engine was never fitted. The wires' positions are measured from the photos (decision 10: 0.1 m)

target.quote: aiming for the number 2 wire is standard operating procedure
target.note: said of CVN 77, whose layout the Ford's follows (dote2025: three wires, as CVN 76 and 77). Where the lens puts the hook on a 3-wire deck is not public; the 2001 LSO NATOPS gives only the 4-wire rule (halfway between the 2 and 3).

runout.quote: Length of deck pendant runout 344 ft (to tail hook)
runout.note: the Mk 7 Mod 3's: the Advanced Arresting Gear's run-out is not public. The flight core stops a trap in this run-out, closed loop to it whatever the weight, speed or thrust, as the gear's controller is (decision 24).

force.quote: Produce a sustained launch force of ~1.3 MN
force.note: the flight core's catapult pulls no more than this

profile.quote: the EMALS is capable of operating within the 1.05 max peak-to-mean acceleration requirement
profile.note: the flight core's catapult is closed loop to the end speed set for the jet, at a constant acceleration once its force has risen (decision 24)

speed.quote: Achieve launch speeds of up to ~100 m/s
speed.note: the end speed the flight core caps a shot at (the ship file's catapults' speed)

catapults.note: two on the bow and two in the waist; their tracks are measured off noaa2022.

lens.note: the shore-training layout's lens face from the ramp lights: a check on the Ford's lens position, not her own value

centreline.quote: The deck centerline markings shall consist of a 3-foot-wide stripe symmetrical about the deck centerline with alternating yellow and white sections
centreline.note: the shore-training form; the Ford's own is measured off noaa2022, which shows the same pattern

sections.quote: The sections shall be 45 feet long beginning with a yellow section
sections.note: the shore-training form; the Ford's own is measured off noaa2022, which shows the same pattern

outer.quote: The outer edge stripes shall be one-foot wide with the outer edge 40 feet from the deck centerline
outer.note: the shore-training form; the Ford's own is measured off noaa2022, which shows the same pattern

inner.quote: The inner edge stripes shall be 3 feet wide with the inner edges 28 feet from the deck centerline
inner.note: the shore-training form; the Ford's own is measured off noaa2022, which shows the same pattern

bars.quote: The two edge stripes shall be connected at 75-foot intervals by 10-foot-wide white bars
bars.note: the shore-training form; the Ford's own is measured off noaa2022, which shows the same pattern

ramp.quote: The ramp athwartship marking is a 10-foot-wide white stripe across the ramp end of the deck
ramp.note: the shore-training form; the Ford's own is measured off noaa2022, which shows the same pattern

colours.value: white, the centreline's sections alternately yellow
colours.quote: The markings shall be non-retroreflective white except for the sections of the centerline markings which are non-retroreflective yellow
colours.note: the paint's colours on the Ford are measured from her photos

markings.note: the Ford's own landing-area markings are measured off noaa2022; navair5150 WP 006 04 gives the shore-training form to compare.

tacan.note: chapter 3: ships' identifiers are two letters. The channel is set per operation and is not public.

layout.about: Placements no source states, in the contract frame (x forward, y up, z starboard, metres; origin on the centreline at the deployed waterline, midway between the flight deck's aft and forward extremes). The deck plan is measured on the orthophotos noaa2022 (primary), noaa2018 and VBMP 2025, each corrected for relief and the grid's scale; their frame F (origin where the centreline meets the stern edge) gives x = F - 165.8585. Each entry says what it was measured on; provisional ones wait for the photo match (stage 5).

notes.deck: height: 18.27 m above the deployed waterline (spread 0.23 m), the raised elevators' top edges against the boot top in three starboard beams (dvids9167788, dvids9142613, dvids7473567) through cameras solved on the deck plan; 18.66 at the starboard bow corner (research/hull). thickness: the edge plate's depth, not measured. outline: 29 corners and joins of robust line fits to the deck edges (noaa2022; 0.1-0.6 m, 1.5-1.9 m at the port bow's transition), the elevators' platforms left out. The starboard quarter's notch: both stern photos (dvids7107228, dvids7107229) show the deck stepping down to a lower platform aft of x -151; its inboard forward corner was the photo match's (-150.8, 22.25), 0.24 m from two photos (research/match), not the orthophoto's (-151.8, 17.0); its forward edge is squared at x -151.3, the sponson's forward end and where the hull's wall begins (references/research/sponsons). texture: about 4.1 cm a texel, square texels. The bow's forward edge checked 2026-11-10 (#80, the photo gate pulled the port bow corner 0.75 m forward): the 2023 overhead (dvids7694421) shows it square across the deck, the end of its white edge line at x 166.67 through that photo's camera (rms 0.03 m over z -12 to 12), 0.41-0.47 m forward of the outline, as the same camera casts the stern's eight sheave housings 0.41 m (sd 0.12) forward of their noaa2022 places; so relative to the wires the bow stands where the outline has it, and the outline is kept. The noaa2022 image itself, forward of its mosaic seam (0.0 +-0.4 along x), ends its bright edge band at 167.2. The starboard edge's plain stretches (2026-11-12, #117, the user: move it): aft of elevator 1 to x -109.1, between the elevators and forward of elevator 2 to the bow's turn, z 36.6, the white edge band's outer side, which the deck research (references/research/deck, starboard_edge) read at 36.5-36.6 and a re-run of its edge profiles at 36.43-36.65 (x -125 to 62), 0.2-0.27 m inside the line fits' 36.64-36.87; the corners moved along the elevators' ends and the bow's turn, the deck-edge lights on those stretches with them; the elevators' outboard sides stay 36.8 (36.77-36.8 in both).
notes.fittings: shuttle: a 1.25 x 0.65 m footprint (±0.2) from catapult 3's at battery in dvids7694421, its top 0.47 of its base's width (dvids9478858, kennedy10011978); its height not measured. deflector (2026-11-09, #63; the user: improve the JBDs up and down, the motion and the holes they sit in): the panel lies in an opening inside the deck's yellow band, which is painted on the deck: Kennedy's raised panels (decision 27) show it on the deck at their base and sides, and the 2023 overhead's bands match the deck markings' lines (deck2), so each opening is that line's inner edge, the layout's earlier rectangles (noaa2018) 0.4-1.1 m too large. Raised 50 ± 3°: the Ford's rise is 0.297 of the panel's width (dvids9455182), which against the opening's depth over width (0.389, the overhead) gives 49.8°. Its face 6 modules across (the face-on Kennedy photo's seams, one per module) by 7 rows of tiles (its row seams at 1810, 2052, 2161, 2284, 2408 px, about one seventh of the face apart), the tan non-skid and soot the deck's paint; its back a grid of box cells, 3 across each module (kennedy_jbd_reddit), to 0.4 (not measured; the free edge's striped band, the face plate, about 0.15); its free edge striped red and white at 45°, about 0.21 m a stripe, and a lug at each module's middle (both Kennedy views; the Ford's edge reads red-brown at dusk). Two struts a module at its middle ±0.026 of the width (deck research), each a thick lower link to a clevis at 0.2 of the rise and a thinner rod to the panel's back at 0.6 of it (kennedy_jbd_reddit): built as a crank from a bearing in the pit and a rod to the back at 0.686 of the panel's depth, each panel's own (catapults' deflector.linkage) searched so that raised the knee stands at 0.25 of the rise and the strut nearly straight, and lowered it folds flat under the panel, never crossing it, in the shallowest pit: 0.95 deep (no photo shows the pit's floor or depth). Its motion (2026-11-09, the user: how long should they take?): the raise measured in DVIDS video 865184 (the Ford's first deployment, 2023, 25 frames a second, a telephoto from aft at dusk), the striped top edge tracked frame by frame from where it rises into the frame (16-21°) to its stop and turned into an angle by the panel's module width in pixels (about 400) and its depth over that width (2.1-2.6, as the deflector is not known): 3.6-3.9 s from 0° to 99% of its travel (3.7 kept), its first 16-21° extrapolated at its first visible rate (18-21° a second); fastest at the start and slowing steadily to its stop as the linkage straightens (half its angle in 0.36 of the time, 94% in 0.8). No video found shows one lowered: one orifice meters the cylinders both ways (NRTC 14310, ch. 5, 'An orifice assembly ... maintains control of fluid flow for both the raising and lowering sequence'), so a lowering runs the raise back at the same pace. The struts and the pit's insides are white and dark as the Kennedy photo shows them. sheave, support, stanchion: see landing. console: the integrated catapult control stations (references/research/iccs): the bow's in the deck between catapults 1 and 2, its lid an elongated hexagon 3.32 x 2.35 m, and the waist's at the port deck edge abeam the waist's 6, its lid a trapezoid 4.31 m outboard and 1.67 m inboard by 1.66, in a well outboard of the edge (its bottom not seen: 16.6, 0.2 m under the catwalk floor it holds, far enough for the depth buffer); each rises out of its surface while its catapults are manned, the bow's 0.7 m (0.6 and 0.8 in two photos), the waist's 0.65 (+-0.2, scaled); the bow's band right outside its lid's rim on every side. antenna: the whips' radius provisional. sheave colour: the tops 1.27-1.53 times the white stripes' in linear light in dvids9478807 (side on, the deck beside it) and 1.5-1.7 times a painted white ring in commons220325-CO784-2240 (overhead): a clean near-white, brighter than the worn stripes (the user, 2026-11-04, from the photo: small white circles); the red triangle on the drum's side facing the wire (fittings.sheave.triangle; 2026-11-13, #125): DVIDS 9405715 (wire 3 port's drum close, Nov 2025) shows it red-brown and worn, apex at the side's foot, its base on the top edge about 0.11 of the diameter wide (75 of ~696 px); by eye, no camera kept for that photo; drawn on every drum's inboard side. sheave arm (2026-11-09, the user: the sheaves lack the fitting on their forward side; rebuilt 2026-11-10, the user: they look strange): a steel bar forward of each rigged housing, a wedge whose solid outboard face falls from under its head to a thin end on the deck, its top 0.24 m wide narrowing to 0.20 by 2.4 m (9405715: 0.24 at 1.8-2.0 m, 0.20 at 2.5-3.3 m); its head beside the housing's outboard side, a plate 2 cm thick lying on the bar's root, a pin and nut through both, over a dark block (the photos show only shadow under the plate). Each arm from its own photo, through cameras solved on its own housing. Wire 3 port (dvids9405715; camera on the housing's rim, the horizon and the pendant, 1.2, 0.9 and 2.2 px, checked on the barricade's flush housing to 0.16 m): its face's foot 20.6° outboard of forward, the bar's middle 0.52 m off the centre's line, its end 3.8 m along; the face 0.060 deep at 1.8 m, 0.047 at 2.3, 0.027 at 2.6, 0.013 at 2.9, 0.006 at 3.25 (each column's top solved above its own foot); the plate's top 0.10. Wire 3 starboard (dvids9478807; camera on the housing's rim and the barricade's flush housing, 2.1 and 1.9 px, its free focal 13008 against the EXIF's 13067): 16.1°, 0.44 m off, its end 2.7 m along (its top's end 2.69, a dark line to 2.75); 0.052 deep at 0.9 m, 0.038 at 1.2, 0.026 at 1.5, 0.02 at 1.75-2.0, 0.011 at 2.26, 0.008 at 2.41; the plate's top 0.085 and its head 0.12 m further aft along its line than port's (its pin and the plate's forward end there). Wires 1 and 2 (commons220325-CO784-2240, its camera's misses at each housing's mark taken out, after which it lays the facts' elevator and dashed lines there within 2 px): straight forward (1.5° and 2.4°), the face's foot 0.24-0.32 m outboard of the centre (the bar's middle 0.5), the dark face to 4.4 and 4.5 m and a faint line on to 5.1 and 5.45 m, the bars' ends; their depth too far off to measure, so wire 3 port's profile stretched to their length (an assumption), the plate's top 0.09; their starboard twins no photo shows, mirrored. The head's plan fitted to both close-ups: in a grazing view a centimetre of height moves a corner 0.1 m, so it holds to about 0.05 m (the starboard plate's forward end 0.06 m long in its photo). The barricade's housings, flush and unrigged, have none. Colour: the bar's top 1.6-1.9 times the deck's in linear light (the island photo). Each rides on its housing, so sinks with it while the wire is not rigged. The first build (2026-11-09) laid a flat strip under a plate floating on a box and mirrored port to starboard; it had been checked only by wireframe positions.
notes.elevators: outline: robust line fits to each platform's four sides (noaa2022; elevator 3's inboard side noaa2018), about 0.1-0.6 m; trapezoids, wider at the deck edge. thickness 1.8 (2026-11-13: the platform's outboard edge, raised, 1.77 m deep cast through dvids9167788's camera and 1.83 through dvids5862257's, its underside's shade below it the head over each doorway), and nothing drives the elevators yet (decision 14). well (2026-11-12, #109): under each platform the hull's flare is cut away to a well, as dvids9167788, dvids9142613 and dvids7473567 show the starboard two and dvids7481395 the port one. rails: the x of the rails the platform runs on, where they meet the hangar deck's sill, cast onto the platform's inboard edge through the photo match's cameras: elevator 1 at -75.37 and -52.62 (dvids9167788), -74.84 and -52.27 (dvids9142613); elevator 2 at 0.10 and 23.20, 0.61 and 23.10; elevator 3 at -117.2 and -94.5 (#119: the middles of their flanges cast onto the wall through dvids5862257's camera at full size, 24 px/m; their feet triangulated in one solve with dvids6015622 and 5862258 at -117.0 and -94.18, +-0.3-0.4; dvids7481395 alone read -116.5). Each well's forward rail stands about 1.1 m forward of the platform's inboard forward corner on the orthophoto, the aft one within 0.25 of its aft corner. The well's ends are taken parallel to the platform's ends (not measured: the photos see them end on or in shadow). hangar: the hangar deck the platform's top comes down to, the openings' sill: 7.65, 7.55, 7.98, 7.89 (dvids9167788) and 7.30, 7.27, 7.19, 7.16 (dvids9142613), so 7.5 (+-0.3; the port camera's 8.3-8.5 read about 0.8 high, as its aperture's top 16.3 against the starboard 15.3). opening: the hangar door's aperture, cut through the well's wall `depth` into the hangar (below: 0.8 until #118), a room 12 m deep reaching 1.5 m past the door's ends and 0.6 over its head, its floor 5 cm under the sill, its back dark (2026-11-12, the user: the holes look simplistic; dvids9167788 and the 2016 James River view, commons160611-james, see the hangar's lit inside through each door; the room's size not measured), at mid-height from x -74.69 to -53.02 and 1.35 to 22.39 (dvids9167788), its top 15.3 (15.28, 15.35), its corners rounded about 3 m (2-3.7 by eye at 13.4 px/m); the port one from the 2019 photos below. Elevator 2's outboard side: 27.05 ± 0.15 m between its half-level ends on noaa2022 (and 27.0 in the photo match), not 85 ft; hiielevator's 85 x 52 ft is one starboard elevator, which elevator 1 (26.0-26.4 m) matches. depth, door and the port opening's ends (2026-11-12, #118; the user: model the doors shut): each doorway is a tunnel through the side, the hangar's door at its inner end (from the hangar, DVIDS 9469028 and the 9 Feb 2024 Norfolk visit on Commons, General_Charles_Q._Brown,_Jr._..._-_12.jpg: a deep frame, no leaves in sight when open). Photos of a door shut: the port one on 8 Apr 2017 (builder's trials), 25 Oct 2019 (leaving the yard: dvids5862257, dvids6015622, dvids5862258) and 8 Aug 2021 (shock trial, commons210808-YD731-1361); both starboard ones on 14 Apr 2017 (commons170414-WZ792-007, their deep aft walls curving in to the door); the one by the island part shut on 7 Nov 2022 (dvids7505008, a leaf from the aft end to about the middle). The three of 2019, full size, solved with the anchors and the model's island, bow and rail points as priors (3.5, 2.3 and 7.8 px rms; 9, 4 and 32 deg aft of abeam): read against the rails in each photo, the door's forward edge and the fitting on its seam move with the camera's bearing as a plane 5.2-5.9 m behind the face would (the bundle alone 6.0-6.8, its oblique camera fitting worst): depth 5.6 (+-0.7); dvids9167788's lit starboard walls reach 3.5-4 m in, a lower bound (the 0.8 m it had would show 0.2-0.3). The port doorway's ends at mid-height read -116.4 and -116.6 aft (dvids5862257, 6015622) and -95.1 forward (+-0.3, all three), so x is those. The leaves slide: in 2019 the door reached the aft end and stood 1.25 m short of the forward one (its edge at -96.35, the rounded end open and dark past it), its seam at -106.2; in 2021 it fills the forward end too (a 1.25 m gap would read a 9 px dark band at its 3 deg, none shows), its seam near the middle (-105.3); in 2017 a joint a third of the way from the forward end. Built shut home: gap 0 at both ends, two equal leaves meeting at the doorway's middle; the fitting on the seam 2.74 m over the sill (2019). The starboard two are taken as the port one. The leaves plain grey and the fitting white by eye (dvids5862257, 24 px/m), the seam 5 cm and the fitting's size by eye. Two short posts on the sill, 1.1 m tall, triangulate on the face rather than the door and are not built. rail, sill and the port blister's ribs (2026-11-13, #119): each rail is a channel on the wall centred on its x, 1.3 m wide (1.29-1.44 cast through dvids5862257's camera, 1.28-1.36 through dvids9167788's), two light flanges and a light web with dark slots between (by eye at 24 px/m, flange and web 0.3), standing out 0.5 by eye (+-0.3: no photo looks along one), its foot a bar 3.5 m up (4.05 and 3.97 under the sill in the two photos), running up under the platform. The well's ends stand half a rail out from the rails' middles, its end walls against their outer flanges, the doorways' ends at their inner flanges (within 0.05 port, 0.1-0.35 starboard). Under the starboard doorways' sills a comb of dark gaps 0.35 wide every 0.7, 0.4 deep from the sill (dvids9167788 at 11-13 px/m, dvids9142613), over x -70.64 to -56.90 and 2.75 to 18.60 cast through dvids9167788's camera (the threshold's finger plates, as DVIDS 8796007 shows them from the hangar); under the port one a curb 0.64 m deep standing out 0.15 by eye, the two posts on it 1.1 m tall at -108.65 and -101.95 (triangulated, above). The port blister ribbed every 1.22 m (dvids5862257, nine ribs), 0.15 wide and deep by eye. frame and vestibule (2026-11-13, #120; the user: the tunnels simplistic): seen from the hangar with the door open (DVIDS 9469028, Dec 2025; 9425210, Nov 2025), the side's rounded opening is framed by a deep ring (lightening holes in it), and behind its inner end a vestibule larger than it, its ceiling a grillage of beams, its walls plain plate, and the hangar wall's own larger rounded opening, where the door shuts. So `depth` is the frame, 3.5 m (the lit frame in dvids9167788 reaches 3.5-4 m in, its far part in shade), the room the vestibule, 2.1 m to the door at 5.6 as measured, in shade (`recess`), reaching 1.0 m past the opening's ends and 0.8 over its head with corners of radius 4.0, two beams 0.5 deep under its ceiling: all by eye from the two views from the hangar, which have no solved camera. commons170414-WZ792-007 shows the starboard doors shut behind deep curved frames with a red-brown edge at their inner end. Plate and room (2026-11-13, the user: the rounded holes thin plates of the hull's thickness, the space behind them rectangular so the rounded parts have a hidden area behind): `depth` is the side plating's thickness, 0.05 (not measured), and the room behind it a rectangle reaching 1.0 past the hole's ends and 0.8 over its head, 5.55 deep to the door (at 5.55, as measured), its walls the hull's grey (shaded by its occlusion), its floor the hangar deck's dark, three beams 0.5 deep under its ceiling (the views from the hangar, by eye). This replaces the 3.5 m frame and 2.1 m vestibule above.
notes.catapults: track: the track's centre traced every metre (noaa2018 band, noaa2022 rails), its ends where the track's signature falls to half (noaa2018, 0.5 m; catapult 3's forward end 1.5 m). battery: 1 m forward of the track's aft end, and stroke: the track less battery and 6 m of braking, inside the 94-103 m the sources give (decision 24): both provisional. deflector: the opening the panel lies in, inside the deck's yellow line (markings catapult_N_deflector_outline, less half its width), its hinge the forward edge, square to the ship, not to the track (the earlier rectangles, fitted to noaa2018 outside the era, ran 0.4-1.1 m outside the 2023 bands).

notes.markings: Measured on noaa2022 in the landing frame: the centreline, the edge stripes' centres and the cross bars' places; widths from the shore standard (markings), which the stripes' measured spacing matches to 3 cm. The centreline's sections: 13.69 m measured (45 ft), yellow from u -6.5 every 27.38 m. notes.openings: hull.crease, hull.boxes, hull.openings (2026-11-13, #123 and #127). Placed by x and height; each cut where the plating's outermost face stands there. The crease (#127): the flare between the profiles and the wells was lofted straight from the knuckle (4.6) to the gallery's foot (15.8, z 36.6); the openings triangulated from those three views lay 1.4-2.6 m inboard of it at 7.6-14.1 m up (the slots at x -79, z 28.79/28.93/29.14 in the three pairs, and the upper slots at -80, 33.20/33.07/32.82, against 30.77 and 35.0), and a line fitted through five heights (7.7, 9.8, 11.1, 11.4, 14.1) rises 1.446 per metre and meets the knuckle's height at 19.1 (the model's knuckle 19.0-19.8): the plating rises straight from the knuckle at that slope to 14.5 (above the upper slots, whose tops reach 14.36), the deck edge's overhang running out from there to the gallery's foot (the dark band under the deck edge in the level beam). From x -113.69 to 28.99, between the aft bay's profile and the forward gallery's; the wells' walls standing on it. Under the island (2026-11-14, #130) the crease holds aft of x -79 (hull.crease.hold): the bend keeps the |z| it has there, the plating straight from the knuckle up to it, where it had narrowed aft with the knuckle line (its z at y 11 from 29.07 at -79 to 27.38 at -112). The features there (the windows, the port, the recess's sill, the three round ports, the slots by elevator 1's aft wall), re-marked in the three views and normalised to y 11 along the slope, lie on one surface from x -112 to -79: the island's minus the round ports' within -0.21 to +0.15 m in every pair of views and in cameras re-solved on the racks, the island's base and elevator 1's edge near it, against the -0.7 the narrowing plating predicted (two of the ports' marks in the bow quarter had sat 5-12 px off them). No block stands proud there: a 0.9 m end face at the recess's forward corner would read 5.5-7.8 px wide in the high beam and the bow quarter, which show a line 2 px wide (a rib), and the knuckle runs on unbroken under it in the high beam; the low view along the side from ahead (dvids9688116) shows no end face either. The 13 P box's face at 32.0 (three views), where 31.3 stood behind the narrowed plating. Each line carried in to the platform's inboard edge and out to the deck's edge, which no view sees (galleries, railings and the deck edge's shade). The rails stand where they were (#119): none against its wall, 0.4-1.05 m from it (the photos show the gap; the midships rail reads 0.52 in the one view that sees it whole, against 0.35).
